title: Inertia depends on energy content

body: Einstein's short 1905 follow-up asks whether a body's inertia depends on its energy content. In the English translation dated 27 September 1905, if a body gives off energy L as radiation, its mass diminishes by L/c². The translation then states a more general conclusion: the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content; if the energy changes by L, the mass changes in the same sense by L/9×10^20, with energy in ergs and mass in grams. That is the relation later written E=mc². The paper presents it as a theoretical conclusion and says it might be tested with bodies whose energy content varies a great deal, such as radium salts. The slogan E=mc² is a later compact notation, not a line of the 1905 title.
